The Confidence Band Widening primitive operates on the principle that uncertainty must increase when new evidence contradicts established priors. In mathematical terms, given a prior belief \(P(	heta)\) and observed data \(D\), the posterior \(P(	heta|D)\) updates via Bayes' theorem. When a signal suggests a player's availability is uncertain (e.g., from injury reports), the variance of the posterior increases, reflecting wider confidence intervals. This prevents overconfident predictions and aligns with the project's guardrail against manufacturing confidence from unreliable sources such as scraped medical data or unlicensed game ratings. The method ensures that any modification to the confidence band is conservative, only widening it based on verifiable public data, thus maintaining honesty in statistical claims.
